notes.meaning: Solomon begins a new section of short sayings that contrast two ways of living. A child who learns wisdom brings great joy to his parents. A child who acts foolishly brings deep sorrow, especially to the mother who cared for him.

Money gained by cheating or stealing does not bring lasting good or true peace. Wealth cannot rescue a person when God judges sin. Living righteously—in an honest way that pleases God—preserves life and removes the terror of death.

The Lord provides for the deepest needs of those who trust and follow Him. Even in hard times, He sustains their souls. At the same time, He blocks the greedy desires of the wicked so that their cravings never bring true satisfaction.

People who are lazy and careless with their work end up poor. On the other hand, steady effort and hard work bring provision and wealth. This truth applies both to everyday jobs and to seeking God with our whole heart.

A sensible person knows the right time to work and gathers crops while the weather is good. Sleeping when the harvest is ready wastes the opportunity and brings public disgrace on the whole family. Wise people make the most of the seasons God gives them.

God pours out real blessings on the upright person, crowning their life with honour. In contrast, wicked people often use smooth words to hide the cruelty they are planning. In the end, their own violent deeds will come back to silence them.

Good people leave behind an honourable name that brings comfort and praise to others long after they die. The wicked leave behind a reputation that decays like rotten wood. People remember evil deeds only with disgust.

Someone with a wise heart is humble enough to welcome God's rules and take good advice. A babbling fool thinks he knows everything and refuses to listen. Because he will not watch his step or hold his tongue, he suddenly falls into ruin.

A person who lives with integrity—being honest and doing what is right—walks through life safely without fear of being unmasked. Anyone who takes crooked paths has to hide what they do. In time, dishonest people are always found out and exposed.
A person who winks secretly to plot harm causes grief to others. At the same time, a foolish talker brings sudden trouble upon himself. Sneaky schemes and reckless words both end in pain.

The speech of a godly person is like a fresh spring that gives life, comfort, and good advice to everyone nearby. By contrast, the mouth of a wicked person hides harmful, violent motives under friendly words. Evil plans bring ruin instead of life.

Hatred is always looking for an excuse to fight and blow small disagreements into big arguments. Love acts differently by forgiving, overlooking offences, and putting out the fire of anger. Choosing love protects peace among families and neighbours.

People who have good understanding show it by speaking wise and helpful words. Those who lack good sense refuse to listen and keep doing foolish things. Since kind words do not reach them, they end up learning hard lessons through painful discipline.

Wise people quietly collect useful knowledge over time and save it for the right moment to speak. A foolish person blurts out careless and hurtful thoughts right away. That kind of reckless talking invites quick destruction.

In everyday life, wealth often shields a person from many earthly troubles, like a strong city wall. Extreme poverty leaves the poor helpless and exposed to disaster. Still, this verse also warns that riches can create false confidence, while poor people need kindness and fair treatment.

An upright person works hard to support his family and help others, which leads to a blessed and peaceful life. The wicked person uses whatever money he gets to fuel selfish desires and sin. Misusing wealth only leads toward guilt and judgment.

Anyone who listens to good teaching and holds onto correction stays on the path to life. But someone who hates being corrected is like a traveller who gets lost and refuses to be shown the right road. Rejecting guidance causes a person to wander further into trouble.

A person who acts friendly while hiding hatred inside is telling lies. It is just as foolish to go around spreading bad reports and slander about others. Both habits show a wicked heart that God will hold accountable.

The more words a person uses, the easier it is to slip into sin, exaggeration, or gossip. Someone who knows when to keep quiet shows true wisdom. Guarding what we say saves us from many painful mistakes.

The words of a righteous person are precious and clean, like pure silver that has been tested in fire. By contrast, the inner thoughts and motives of a wicked person have almost no value at all. What comes out of our mouths shows what our hearts are truly worth.

A godly person's words feed and strengthen many people with truth, just like a shepherd feeding a flock. Fools, however, bring about their own ruin because they refuse to think or learn. While the wise help others live, fools destroy themselves.

True and lasting wealth comes from the Lord's blessing, not just from human striving. When God gives, He does not add the painful regret, guilt, or bitter anxiety that come from ill-gotten gain. His gifts bring peace and content to the heart.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some popular teachers claim this verse promises financial riches and an easy, trouble-free life to every believer who has enough faith.

notes.meaning: A foolish person treats doing wrong like a game or a joke, laughing off the harm he causes. A person with understanding finds his joy in acting wisely and doing what is right. What amuses us reveals what kind of character we have.

Even when wicked people act fearless, they carry secret fears of judgment, and those very terrors will catch up with them. The righteous desire what is pleasing to God, and He will give them what their hearts long for. God answers according to our trust, not our fears.

Wicked people may seem powerful, but when the storm of God's judgment blows through, they are swept completely away. The righteous person is built on an everlasting foundation and stays secure. Trusting God gives us stability that outlasts every trial.

Sour vinegar hurts the teeth, and thick smoke stings the eyes and makes them tear up. A lazy worker does the exact same thing to the person who sends him on a task. Trusting an unreliable person brings nothing but frustration and disappointment.

Living with reverent respect for the Lord generally protects a person from destructive habits and leads to a full life. In contrast, wicked living often cuts a person's years short through violence and foolish choices. Honoring God is the best foundation for a long and healthy life.

The patient hope of the righteous leads to gladness because God will fulfill what they are waiting for. The wicked expect great things for themselves, but all their dreams will vanish when they die. Real hope is found only in God.

Walking in the Lord's ways serves as a strong fortress for people who live with integrity. That very same holy way brings fear and destruction to those who practice evil. God's truth protects the obedient but breaks those who oppose it.

Those who walk with God have a secure standing that will never be permanently shaken. Wicked people may enjoy earthly things for a short time, but they have no lasting home in the land. God keeps His people safe forever.

A good person's mouth produces wise and helpful words, like a healthy plant bringing forth good fruit. A twisted tongue that constantly spreads lies and rebellion will be cut off. God will not let deceitful words go unpunished forever.

Righteous people know what is pleasing to God and helpful to their listeners, and that is what they choose to say. Wicked people only know how to speak what is twisted, bitter, and hurtful. A wise person uses words to build others up.
